title: Build a Balanced Meal from Label Clues

callouts.label: Start with the Serving Information
callouts.hint: The blank ruled panel on the tall blue package at the far left.
callouts.description: On a real package, serving information tells what amount the rest of the label describes.
callouts.ap_tip: If a person eats a different amount, the nutrient totals change too.

callouts.label: Whole-Grain Carbohydrate
callouts.hint: The large seeded loaf in the front-left foreground.
callouts.description: Whole-grain foods can provide carbohydrates for energy along with fiber.
callouts.ap_tip: Balance is about a mix of jobs, not one perfect food.

callouts.label: Colorful Produce
callouts.hint: The large crate of varied vegetables across the left foreground.
callouts.description: Fruits and vegetables can contribute fiber, vitamins, minerals, color, and texture.
callouts.ap_tip: Cultural and seasonal choices can fill this role in many ways.

callouts.label: Beans and Lentils
callouts.hint: The small bowl of multicolored beans near the front center.
callouts.description: Beans and lentils can contribute protein, carbohydrate, fiber, vitamins, and minerals.
callouts.ap_tip: One food can support more than one nutrient job.

callouts.label: Calcium-Rich Choice
callouts.hint: The white bowl near the center-left of the counter.
callouts.description: Dairy foods and fortified alternatives can contribute calcium and other nutrients.
callouts.ap_tip: Labels help compare alternatives because products vary.

callouts.label: Fats with Useful Jobs
callouts.hint: The walnuts and avocado on the wooden board in the center.
callouts.description: Nuts, seeds, avocado, and oils provide fats that support energy storage, protection, and vitamin absorption.
callouts.ap_tip: The body needs fats; the goal is variety and balance.

callouts.label: Water for Hydration
callouts.hint: The clear water pitcher near the center-right.
callouts.description: Water supports temperature control, transport, joints, and waste removal.
callouts.ap_tip: It is a useful everyday beverage before, during, and after activity.

callouts.label: Another Grain Choice
callouts.hint: The brown bowl of cooked grains behind the water pitcher.
callouts.description: Rice, oats, corn, breads, noodles, and other grains can be part of a balanced meal.
callouts.ap_tip: A balanced meal does not need to match one culture or one picture.

callouts.label: Protein Variety
callouts.hint: The fish and tofu plate on the right side of the table.
callouts.description: Fish, tofu, eggs, beans, lentils, meat, nuts, dairy, and alternatives can contribute protein.
callouts.ap_tip: Different families build protein choices in different ways.

callouts.label: Fruit and Vegetable Mix
callouts.hint: The colorful shared bowl at the lower right.
callouts.description: A variety of fruits and vegetables brings different tastes, textures, and micronutrients.
callouts.ap_tip: Variety across time matters more than making every plate identical.

callouts.label: Treats Can Fit
callouts.hint: The small square dessert at the far lower-right edge.
callouts.description: A treat can be part of eating without becoming the foundation of the meal.
callouts.ap_tip: Health education should support flexible choices rather than guilt.

callouts.label: Compare, Ask, and Choose
callouts.hint: The child and trusted adult comparing two packages in the center.
callouts.description: Labels are evidence tools, and a trusted adult can help interpret unfamiliar ingredients or claims.
callouts.ap_tip: Use evidence together with family needs, culture, access, allergies, and preferences.
